description: Physical land references are independent of political continuity. Components are selected whole, never cut to a bounding rectangle; missing coverage is computed against each snapshot. Ownership is explicit and time bounded; null means geographical land only, not an inferred polity.

regions.name: Solomon archipelago
regions.note: Archipelago includes territories of more than one modern state. Do not assign the whole archipelago to a single country.

regions.name: Vanuatu / New Hebrides
regions.note: Before independence on 1980-07-30 this was an Anglo-French condominium; leave sovereignty unspecified rather than copying the upstream France-only claim.

regions.name: New Caledonia
regions.note: French administration across the selected modern snapshots; geographical identity is distinct from the controlling polity.

regions.name: Russian Arctic islands
regions.note: Whole island components only; mainland components extending outside the window are excluded. Does not extend historical ownership back to 1920 or earlier.

regions.name: Chukotka east of the date line
regions.note: The western-longitude component is a separate GeoJSON polygon, not a missing arbitrary corner to be drawn by hand.

regions.name: Southern Kuril Islands
regions.note: Physical islands only. These four southern island groups have disputed sovereignty; keep the missing 1960 coverage neutral rather than invent a sovereign claim.

regions.name: Northern Kuril Islands
regions.note: Northern chain, outside the four southern groups claimed by Japan. USSR control in 1960; Russian Federation after 1991.

regions.name: Southern Korean peninsula and coastal islands
regions.note: Joseon-era coastal land, after Tamna incorporation. The reference is the detailed unnamed southern-peninsula geometry already present in the 1600 source, corroborated by the later southern-peninsula geometry. Assign only geometrically identical existing unnamed coverage AND only when the snapshot already identifies Korea. Preserve that snapshot native political evidence; do not copy any modern-state identity or change the northern land border.
